headline: OpenAI partners with Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL to enhance AI-driven journalism in Brazil.

items.title: OpenAI, Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL announce strategic content partnership
items.summary: OpenAI has entered a partnership with Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL to integrate trusted Brazilian journalism into ChatGPT. This collaboration aims to enhance access to reliable news with clear attribution and transparency, expanding the reach and utility of AI in the media sector. The partnership will allow users to receive news from these reputable sources directly via ChatGPT, potentially improving the quality of information dissemination in Portuguese-speaking regions.
items.why_it_matters: AI developers need to consider content partnerships for enhancing AI model accuracy and user trust.

items.title: OpenBrief – Local-first video downloader/summarizer
items.summary: OpenBrief is a GUI tool built on yt-dlp with integrated AI capabilities, enabling local video downloads and AI-driven transcriptions and summaries. Users can input a video link to download and process media content locally, leveraging their own AI keys. As an open-source tool, it offers a blend of video management with AI, enhancing local data processing capabilities.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit
items.summary: This toolkit provides policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, execution sandboxing, and reliability engineering for autonomous AI agents. It addresses the OWASP Agentic Top 10, aiming to enhance security and governance in deploying AI agents.

items.title: Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models
items.summary: A recent study on arXiv investigates how LLMs' confidence levels often exceed their actual accuracy across diverse tasks. This research highlights the need for improved calibration in LLMs to enhance their reliability in real-world applications.

all_items.title: LQ-rPPG: A Label-Quantized Coarse-to-Fine Learning Framework for Remote Physiological Measurement
all_items.summary: arXiv:2605.23174v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables non-contact measurement of physiological signals from facial videos, offering strong potential for remote healthcare and daily health monitoring. Driven by this potential, various deep learning-based rPPG methods have been proposed to improve rPPG estimation. However, previous deep learning-based rPPG methods have paid little attention to the quality of training labels and their impact on model learning.
